run.question: Debug memory issues for my Python application orca in namespace app-95

report.summary: The orca Python workload in namespace app-95 is being OOMKilled because its own process retains every processed image and every thumbnail without any bound. The single pod orca-57fdcbf45f-knnnc (ReplicaSet orca-57fdcbf45f, Deployment orca) is Running and ready but its container 'orca' has restartCount 1 with lastState terminated reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137 at 2026-11-21T07:22:57Z, and the Deployment limit is memory 128Mi. The previous container's logs show a strictly growing store: 'Cache size: N thumbnails' and 'Memory usage: processed_images list has N items' rise together, with 'Approximate memory used by stored images' going 13.9 MB at 10 images, 59.6 MB at 50, 109.0 MB at 90 and 120.3 MB at 100 images, after which the process was killed; startup lines state the configuration is 'Storing all processed images for audit trail' and 'Caching thumbnails for quick retrieval', i.e. no eviction. The restarted container repeated exactly the same ramp from zero (62.9 MB by 50 images at 07:23:03), so this is unbounded retention, not gradual drift, and recurrence is expected while the limit stays at 128Mi. Checked and not the cause: namespace app-95 has no configuration object other than kube-root-ca.crt, and the node reports MemoryPressure False with ~32.9 GiB allocatable, so neither an injected retention/fault setting nor node memory pressure explains it. The actual defect lives in the application source, mounted from Secret 'app-code' at /app, whose contents I could not read; Prometheus was unreachable so container memory/working-set metrics could not be checked. Conclusion is supported by pod status, deployment/ReplicaSet specs, previous-container logs and node conditions; the code-level line and a memory-growth metric are the remaining unknowns.

claims.text: Pod orca-57fdcbf45f-knnnc in namespace app-95 is owned by ReplicaSet orca-57fdcbf45f, is Running with phase Running and its container 'orca' ready, has restartCount 1, and its container lastState is terminated with reason OOMKilled and exitCode 137 finishedAt 2026-11-21T07:22:57Z (startedAt 2026-11-21T07:22:26Z); pod startTime is 2026-11-21T07:22:25Z on node opspilot-m1-control-plane.

Deployment app-95/orca runs one replica of container 'orca' (image python:3.9-slim, command ['python','/app/app.py'], env PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 and SERVICE_NAME=orca-image-processor) with resources.limits.memory=128Mi and requests cpu=10m/memory=64Mi, and Deployment status shows 1/1 ready at 2026-11-21T07:22:58Z.

Only one ReplicaSet exists for the workload — orca-57fdcbf45f, owner Deployment orca, created 2026-11-21T07:22:25Z, 1/1 ready, same container image python:3.9-slim and same 128Mi memory limit — so the container restart happened inside one unchanged pod template, not through a new ReplicaSet generation.

The previous container instance logged 'Configuration: Storing all processed images for audit trail' and 'Configuration: Caching thumbnails for quick retrieval' at startup, and then a monotonically growing store: 'Cache size: 10 thumbnails'/'Memory usage: processed_images list has 10 items'/'Approximate memory used by stored images: 13.9 MB' (07:22:27), 59.6 MB at 50 items (07:22:31), 109.0 MB at 90 items (07:22:51), and '120.3 MB' at 100 items (07:22:56), with 'Batch complete: processed images 76 to 100' at 07:22:57 and then no further lines from that instance.

The restarted container (started 2026-11-21T07:22:58) logged the same startup configuration lines and the same ramp from zero: 12.0 MB at 10 items (07:22:59), 36.0 MB at 30 items (07:23:01), 51.2 MB at 40 items (07:23:02), 62.9 MB at 50 items (07:23:03), i.e. roughly 1.2 MB of retained image data per processed image.

Namespace app-95 contains exactly one ConfigMap, kube-root-ca.crt, and it holds only the cluster CA bundle — no retention, cache-size, memory or fault-injection setting exists in ConfigMaps for this workload.

The orca application code is not in the image but mounted into /app from a Secret named app-code (deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=1, RollingUpdate strategy, no nodeSelector); the Secret's value is credential-redacted and could not be read, so the program source itself was not inspected.

Node opspilot-m1-control-plane reports MemoryPressure=False with reason KubeletHasSufficientMemory, DiskPressure=False, PIDPressure=False, Ready=True, and 32859944Ki allocatable memory, so the node was not under memory pressure when checked.

The event view for the authorized window returned six events, all in namespace app-95 and all between 2026-11-21T07:22:25Z and 2026-11-21T07:22:57Z: Deployment ScalingReplicaSet (1), ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate (1), and Pod Created, Scheduled, Pulled and Started (1 each); no pod-eviction or OOMKilling event appeared in that returned set.

Primary cause: the orca process keeps an unbounded in-memory store — the processed_images list plus a thumbnail cache with no eviction — so resident memory rises about 1.2 MB per image and crosses the Deployment's 128Mi container limit after roughly 100 images (~31 s of processing in the first run), which the kubelet then enforces by OOM-killing PID 1 (exit 137). This rests on the log-reported growth and the OOMKilled lastState, not on a memory metric, because Prometheus was unreachable.

Secondary candidate, not separable from the first: the 128Mi memory limit (request 64Mi) is too small for the application's configured behaviour of storing all processed images and caching thumbnails; if the retention behaviour were intended, only raising the limit would postpone the kill, since growth is linear and unbounded.

Rejected: a fault-injection or memory/cache setting applied to this workload from configuration. The only ConfigMap in app-95 is kube-root-ca.crt (CA bundle) and the Deployment's env holds only PYTHONUNBUFFERED and SERVICE_NAME, so no setting was found that injects the retention behaviour; the retention is recorded by the application's own startup log lines.

Rejected: node-level memory pressure causing the kill. The only node, opspilot-m1-control-plane, reports MemoryPressure=False (KubeletHasSufficientMemory) and ~32.9 GiB allocatable, while the kill hit a single container whose own logged retained-image estimate had just reached 120.3 MB against a 128Mi container limit.

Rejected: the restart was a rollout/reschedule by the Deployment. There is a single ReplicaSet orca-57fdcbf45f (created 07:22:25Z) with the same image and 128Mi limit, no second ReplicaSet generation, and the pod itself was not replaced — restartCount 1 with the container lastState terminated OOMKilled, so the same pod's container was restarted in place.

Fix the retention in the application source (the /app code mounted from Secret app-code): cap the processed_images audit store (collections.deque(maxlen=N) or periodic flush) and give the thumbnail cache a size/TTL bound, since both grow per image and together drive the container past 128Mi in about 30 seconds of processing.

As a stopgap only, raise Deployment orca's container memory limit above the measured peak (the logged retained-image estimate alone reached 120.3 MB at 100 images and the Python runtime adds its own overhead) and, once Prometheus is reachable, confirm the actual container working set against the limit rather than relying on the app's own estimate.

gaps: The application source could not be read: it is mounted into /app from a Secret named app-code, and Secret contents are not readable in this Run, so the exact code path retaining objects (list append vs cache dict) is inferred from the app's own log output, not inspected.

No container memory metric was obtainable: two get_metric_names calls to Prometheus (patterns .*memory.* and .*container_memory.*, 2026-11-21T06:30:00Z–07:23:04Z and 07:00:00Z–07:23:04Z) returned status error SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so the real working-set curve, RSS at kill time and any earlier memory history are unknown rather than zero.

Cluster/application data begins at 2026-11-21T07:22:25Z (earliest pod, ReplicaSet and event timestamps), so behaviour before that time — including whether earlier pods of this Deployment were also OOMKilled — is unknown; earlier logs of a pod that no longer exists cannot be read.

Whether the restarted container has since been OOM-killed again was not determined: the pod query at 07:23:06Z showed restartCount 1 and the current instance still running, and log evidence stops at 07:23:03Z inside the authorized window.

No impact outside this workload can be assessed: no Service, Ingress or caller errors for orca were checked, and with Prometheus unavailable no error-rate or latency baseline exists for comparison; nothing observed shows downstream or customer impact.

Change history is not an integrated data source in this Run, so when the Deployment was created or whether its memory limit was ever changed is unknown; only the current single-revision state (deployment.kubernetes.io/revision=1) is visible.
next_steps: Read orca's source (the app.py file inside Secret app-code, via the deploy pipeline's source repository rather than the cluster) and locate the processed-images list and thumbnail cache to confirm the unbounded retention noted in its own log lines.

Once Prometheus is reachable again, query container memory working set for namespace app-95, pod orca-57fdcbf45f-knnnc, container orca against kube_pod_container_resource_limits to size the limit from real data instead of the app's 'Approximate memory used by stored images' estimate.
If the audit trail must be kept, move it out of process memory (write/rotate to disk or object storage) and keep only a bounded in-memory window so a restart is not required to reclaim memory.
